proofs.proof_tex:
All variables in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\},
\]
so every local entry is rational and strictly between zero and one, as required by \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\).  The table for \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\); the table for \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\); the table for \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\); and the table for \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Thus every displayed parent is active and the parent relations are exactly those of \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

Marginalizing \(U_i\) produces the directed edge \(X_i\to Y_i\) and the bidirected edge \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) induced by \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the other displayed arrows have no latent internal vertex and remain.  Every other path has an observed internal vertex, so it creates no additional latent-projection edge.  This gives precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  In the selected projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the adjacent endpoint marks are tails.  The pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) and \((Y_i,C_i)\) are adjacent.  The remaining pair is nonadjacent: in the ancestral moral graph for \(\{X_i,C_i,Y_i,S_i\}\), after conditioning on and removing \(Y_i,S_i\), the vertex \(C_i\) is disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.                 \tag{7}
\]
The three-node noncollider chain has no invariant endpoint mark in its input-free equivalence class.  Its completed partial graph is therefore
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}
 =X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i
       \mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i,
\]
and the direct projection checks give
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \quad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \quad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}. \tag{8}
\]
Together with binary support from \(\text{ass:binary-certificate-support}\), positivity and rationality, (8) and \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) imply
\[
 \mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}). \tag{9}
\]

We next compute the unselected base laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\), Bayes' rule, with the positive denominators displayed below, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{10}
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), iterated expectation and the outcome table in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
   \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a)\right\}
   P(U_i=u\mid X_i=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12.                 \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equations (10)--(11) show that both signs have the same base observational law, with
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for every }a,b\in\{0,1\}.                  \tag{12}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), modularity deletes the factor for \(X_i\) but leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}. \tag{13}
\end{aligned}
\]

The appended tables are the concrete instance of \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\) with
\[
 g_b(d):=P(C_i=d\mid Y_i=b),
 \qquad \lambda_0=\lambda_1:=\frac3{16},
 \qquad \Lambda=\frac38.                                \tag{14}
\]
Indeed, for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 g_b(d)P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b,C_i=d)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{15}
\]
Moreover \(0<3/16<1/4=\min_b g_b(d)\).  Both new parent relations are active, as already checked before (7), so the graph qualification of the equalizer lemma is also satisfied.  Applying its observational identity to (12) gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac14\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.                         \tag{16}
\]
Summing (16) over the eight observed cells gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8\); dividing by this positive normalizer gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{17}
\]
Thus the two full selected observational laws agree and have full support.

The interventional identities of \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\), (13), and (14) give both selection normalizers as \(3/8\) and give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac12,\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac9{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac9{32},\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac7{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac7{32}.    \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The common denominator in (18) is positive, so division gives selected conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\).  Directly from the common \(C_i\) table,
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14
 =P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),                                   \tag{19}
\]
which proves that the connected conditioning coordinate is informative before selection.

For the graphical obstruction, \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Directly,
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},
 \qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.          \tag{20}
\]
After intervention on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) remains an ancestor of the terminal set: it belongs to that set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Hence
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{21}
\]
It remains to verify the maximal selection-exchange coordinate rather than infer it from the absence of an input vertex in the original graph.  Since \(S=\{S_i\}\), the only nonempty candidate is \(D=\{S_i\}\).  In the corresponding input-augmented graph, the length-two path
\[
 I_{S_i}\longrightarrow S_i\longleftarrow C_i           \tag{22}
\]
is open when conditioning on \(S_i\): its sole internal vertex is a conditioned collider, and there is no noncollider on the path that could block it.  Thus \(I_{S_i}\) and \(C_i\) fail the required id-separation, so \(\{S_i\}\) is inadmissible.  The empty set is admissible vacuously and is the only remaining subset; consequently its unique maximal value is
\[
 D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing.                     \tag{23}
\]
The bidirected-connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and maximal-exchange checks (20)--(23) are the terminal selected-hedge predicates in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  Therefore \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge.

Finally, form \(\widetilde P\) by changing only
\(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The new entry and its complement are positive rational numbers.  At fixed \(C_i=0\), the selection table still changes with \(Y_i\), and at fixed \(Y_i=0\), it still changes with \(C_i\); hence both arrows into \(S_i\) remain active and the represented graph is unchanged.  Equations (10)--(12) are unchanged, so the two signs still have the same unselected observed law.  Because their \(C_i\) and modified \(S_i\) kernels are also common, factorization gives identical selected observational masses, and therefore identical full selected observational laws, for the two signs.

Put \(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\).  For \(Y_i=0\), summing the unchanged products in (15) gives \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=0)=3/8\).  For \(Y_i=1\), the \(C_i=0\) product remains \(3/16\), while the modified \(C_i=1\) product is \((3/4)(1/2)=3/8\); hence \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=9/16\).  It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 \widetilde P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.            \tag{24}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first quantity in (24) is positive.  Therefore the modified selected denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma(1;0)
 =\frac{3+3p}{6+3p}=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.                    \tag{25}
\]
Substitution of \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (13) yields
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},
 \qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39},                         \tag{26}
\]
and these fractions are unequal because \(25\cdot39=975\ne943=23\cdot41\).  Thus the denominator equality in (18) is the tuned informative cancellation furnished by (14)--(15), not a consequence of the represented graph.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal W\) be a finite observed vector containing a treatment subvector \(\mathcal X\) and a single finite outcome vertex \(\mathcal Y\).  Let \(\mathbf Q_0\) and \(\mathbf Q_1\) be finite SCMs with positive rational local tables such that \(P_0(\mathcal W=w)=P_1(\mathcal W=w)\) for every observed cell \(w\), but, for some assignments \(x,y\),
\[
 P_0(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 \ne
 P_1(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)).
\]
Append binary vertices \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal S\), driven by private exogenous variables independent of the old exogenous variables, and use the same new kernels in both SCMs.  For rational numbers \(g_u(c)\) satisfying \(g_u(c)>0\) and \(\sum_{c=0}^1g_u(c)=1\) for every outcome value \(u\), choose rational \(\lambda_c\) such that
\[
 0<\lambda_c<\min_u g_u(c),
 \qquad c\in\{0,1\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda:=\lambda_0+\lambda_1,
\]
and set
\[
 P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)=g_u(c),
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)
   =\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}.
\]
Then the two extended SCMs are positive and rational and, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c,\\
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda},\\
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
     \frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the full selected observational laws and every positive conditioning denominator agree, whereas the displayed selected joint numerators and conditional causal effects disagree.  Graph membership has the following conditional form only: if the two base SCMs have a common represented graph \(\mathcal H\), if \(g_u(\cdot)\) is nonconstant in \(u\), and if \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) is nonconstant in \(c\) for at least one fixed \(u\), then every proposed parent is active and both extensions have the common represented graph obtained from \(\mathcal H\) by adjoining \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal C\), \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S\), and \(\mathcal C\to\mathcal S\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(0<\lambda_c<g_u(c)\), both
\(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) and its complement lie strictly between zero and one.  All new table entries are rational, so appending the two private-noise mechanisms preserves positivity and rationality.  Also,
\[
 0<\Lambda=\sum_{c=0}^1\lambda_c
 <\sum_{c=0}^1g_u(c)=1.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Appending children does not change the old marginal law.  If the outcome component of \(w\) is \(u\), the SCM factorization and the two displayed new kernels give, for each \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)
   P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)
   P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)g_u(c)\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c.                              \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The division in (2) is legitimate because \(g_u(c)>0\).  Summing (2) over \(w\) and \(c\) yields \(P_j(\mathcal S=1)=\Lambda\); hence equality of the two old observational laws implies equality of the two normalized full selected observational laws,
\[
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal S=1)
 =P_j(\mathcal W=w)\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.              \tag{3}
\]

Under \(\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)\), modularity leaves both appended child mechanisms unchanged.  Summing out the old variables other than \(\mathcal Y\) in the analogue of (2) gives
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1
      \mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 =P_j(\mathcal Y=u\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
  \lambda_c.                                               \tag{4}
\]
Summing (4) over \(u,c\), over \(u\), and then dividing by the positive quantity \(\Lambda\) from (1), respectively, proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda},\\
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
     \frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.                           \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator in the second line of (5) is common and positive.  The strictly positive multiplier \(\lambda_c/\Lambda\) in the third line shows that the assumed interventional disagreement gives unequal joint numerators.  Dividing the third line by the second shows that the selected conditional effect is exactly the old effect,
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),
       \mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 =P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)),   \tag{6}
\]
so the effects disagree as well.

For the final graph assertion, independent private exogenous variables and the displayed kernels add no parent other than the displayed old outcome and new conditioning vertex.  Nonconstancy of \(g_u(\cdot)\) in \(u\) makes \(\mathcal Y\) active for \(\mathcal C\).  Since every \(\lambda_c>0\), the same nonconstancy makes \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) nonconstant in \(u\) for some fixed \(c\), so \(\mathcal Y\) is active for \(\mathcal S\); the last stated hypothesis makes \(\mathcal C\) active for \(\mathcal S\).  Thus, under the explicitly stated common-base-graph and active-parent hypotheses, both extensions have exactly the claimed common represented extension.  No graph-membership conclusion was used without those hypotheses.
added_lemmas.justification: The lift converts an ordinary positive rational causal witness into a denominator-locked selected conditional witness by a constructive common child and selection mechanism.
added_lemmas.gap: An ordinary hedge pair need not preserve a selected conditioning denominator, so an explicit equalizing construction is required.
added_lemmas.consumer: The informative table proposition instantiates this lift, and future graphical synthesis may use it whenever a common represented base witness is available.

proposed.statement: The mechanisms in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are strictly positive and rational and induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), whose latent projections are \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i\), with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\})\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}\). Both models therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\). Moreover \(P_{\sigma}(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)=r_a\) and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)=1/2\), while \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\). Hence \(P_{\sigma}(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)=3/64\), \(P_{\sigma}(S_i=1)=3/8\), and the two full selected observational laws assign probability \(1/8\) to every observed cell. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), \(P_+(Y_i=1)=9/16\), \(P_-(Y_i=1)=7/16\), and both selection normalizers equal \(3/8\). At the root role state, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1;0)=1/2\), whereas \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)=9/32\) and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)=7/32\), so the conditional effects are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\). The connected \(C_i\) is informative before selection because \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\neq1/4=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)\). The pair \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) consists of nested \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\)-rooted C-forests, with \(V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\})\); \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\), so they form the terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\). Finally, replacing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) by \(1/2\) preserves the graph and equality of the two selected observational laws but yields denominators \(25/41\) and \(23/39\); therefore the displayed denominator equality is a tuned informative cancellation, not a structural consequence of the graph.
proposed.justification: The proposition instantiates the general selection-equalizer lift with informative common child and selection kernels, verifies the represented graph and terminal forest, and exhibits exact positive locked denominators with separated numerators.
proposed.gap: Selected hedges alone do not coordinate the conditioning denominator; this example supplies a connected exact instance and a same-graph perturbation proving that the equality is tuned rather than forced by separation.
proposed.consumer: The table is a positive-control certificate for rational selected-hedge synthesis and verifies the general equalizer formulas with exact arithmetic.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The revised proof uses the paper-owned selection-equalizer lemma, so the proposition must record that load-bearing dependency.

prose_updates.tldr: Branch-sCIDP is a direct published-class soundness specialization and finite formula search, not a new completeness theorem. A general selection-equalizer lift now converts any two positive rational finite SCMs with the same observational law but different ordinary interventional outcome laws into selected models with the same full selected observational law, a common positive conditioning denominator, and different joint numerators and conditional effects. The connected binary table is an exact instance, while the affine rank compiler gives a second exact construction for a supplied represented family. Whether every all-branches failure yields a represented locked construction remains open.

project_justification.gap: Failure of selected joint identification does not by itself preserve the conditioning denominator, and the published conditional algorithm supplies soundness rather than selected conditional completeness. Ordinary selected hedges therefore leave a genuine graph-to-lock construction problem.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates three levels cleanly: the published positive-discrete Branch-sCIDP soundness result, exact algebraic or equalizer constructions of denominator-locked rational witnesses, and the still-open graphical implication from universal branch failure to one of those constructions.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a general constructive selection-equalizer lift, an exact affine rank compiler for a supplied represented model family, and a connected positive rational binary instance with a same-graph perturbation showing that locking is tuned rather than graph-imposed. The residual forest-to-lock implication is retained as an open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model, complete unconditional sIDP, and sound conditional sCIDP. Branch-sCIDP is presented only as a direct input-free-COPAG specialization and exhaustive restatement of that published soundness architecture. Their unconditional residual forests motivate the open graph-to-lock question but do not establish denominator locking. Abouei and coauthors study selected hedges for an unconditional selected intervention target in a known augmented graph, whereas the present equalizer and rank constructions coordinate a postintervention conditioning denominator. Shpitser and Pearl and, without selection, Jaber and coauthors provide the fixed-graph and PAG conditional benchmarks that motivate exhaustive role exchange. Duarte and coauthors motivate exact finite discrete fiber computation; the present rational constructions target checkable nonidentification certificates rather than sharp-bound optimization.
prose_updates.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Branch-sCIDP soundness is stated over the published positive discrete class, whereas the explicit affine and equalizer countermodels lie in its positive rational binary subclass; a countermodel pair in that subclass refutes identification in the larger class, but this negative transfer supplies no positive completeness implication. The equalizer's graph-membership conclusion applies only when the base pair has a common represented graph and the appended parent relations are active. The affine rank equivalence is conditional on a specified perturbation interval that remains in the represented class. The connected table proves nonvacuity and the same-graph perturbation proves that its lock is not structural. The implication from all reachable terminal failures to a represented residual forest with a locked rational pair, together with the advertised synthesis bound, remains exactly the graph-to-lock open question. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only claims, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness are outside scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
For a represented model \(\mathbf M\), write
\[
 \mathcal X_A(\mathbf M)
 :=\prod_{v\in A}\operatorname{supp}_{\mathbf M}(V_v)
\]
for the finite discrete state space of an observed set \(A\subseteq V\); for
\(A=\varnothing\) this is the singleton containing the empty assignment.  Put
\(W=X\cup C\).  If \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) is a role state, let
\(\bar x\) and \(\bar c\) be the restrictions of the original assignment
\((x,c)\) to \(\bar X\) and \(\bar C\), respectively, and define the
proof-local kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid \operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
 \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
 \tag{1}
\]
The sets in (1) are well typed and disjoint: by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\),
\(Y\cap W=\varnothing\), and by the definition of a role state,
\(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W\).  The model hypothesis
\(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\)
places \(\mathbf M\) in \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Thus all discrete
point masses used below are pointwise versions, and, at each assignment under
consideration,
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}(\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
When \(\bar C=\varnothing\), the corresponding conditional mass after
conditioning on \(S=\mathbf 1\) is one.  Equation (2) is the positivity premise
needed for every conditioning and division below.

We first establish invariance along every edge of the role graph.  At its root
\(\rho_0=(X,C)\), \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{3}
\]
Suppose an edge from \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) moves the nonempty current
bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning.
By \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\), that edge exists
only if its Rule--2 separation holds.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
These four sets are pairwise disjoint by the role partition and
\(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  The Rule--2 equality is therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(
 Y=y\mid T=\bar x_T,\bar C=\bar c,
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=\bar x_{\bar X\setminus T}),
 S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
If instead an edge moves nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to
treatment, apply the same lemma with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality in the reverse direction gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \tag{5}
\]
Induction on the finite number of edges in a trace, using (3)--(5), yields
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \quad\text{for every reachable }\rho.
 \tag{6}
\]

Now suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds at
\(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  The terminal sIDP call has outcome set
\(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  They are disjoint,
and \(A_0\ne\varnothing\) by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  The pointwise positive-discrete
specialization in \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\) therefore gives
\[
 F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)
 \quad
 \text{for all }y\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M).
 \tag{7}
\]
This invocation is directly on \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); it does not
infer positive identification from the binary rational certificate subclass.
Finite support marginalization of (7), followed by the corrected definition
of \(D_\rho\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})\\
 &\qquad=\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\\
 &\qquad=P_{\mathbf M}(\bar C=\bar c
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1)
 =D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
where the final inequality is (2) after division by the positive selection
mass.  Dividing (7) by (8), applying the definition of conditional
probability, and then using (6), we obtain
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'\in\mathcal X_Y(\mathbf M)}
   F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the normalized expression is an observed-law identifying map for the
causal target; equality was derived from Rule--2 and sIDP soundness and was not
introduced as a definition.  No division is attempted when sIDP fails.

It remains to establish the finite-search and cache bounds.  A role state is
uniquely determined by \(\bar X\subseteq W\), because
\(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Hence
\[
 |\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)|\le 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
 \tag{10}
\]
A nonrepeating trace with \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so (10)
implies a maximum trace length of \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\).

For the outer enumeration, each visited state tests at most two directions for
each of at most \(n\) buckets.  The manipulated graph has \(O(n)\) observed
and regime vertices and \(O(n^2)\) marked adjacencies.  The required
separation test is a reachability search on the finite graph of admissible
edge-incidence states, and anterior closure, bucket construction, and region
construction are likewise finite graph searches.  Each test therefore costs
\(\operatorname{poly}(n)\), so the outer search costs
\[
 O\!\left(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{11}
\]

By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\), a deterministic
BuildTree subproblem is keyed by one subset \(R\subseteq V\), while a fixing
subproblem is keyed by a pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  There are at
most \(2^n\) keys of the first kind, and
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}
 =(1+2)^n=3^n.
 \tag{12}
\]
The equality in (12) also follows by assigning each vertex independently to
\(R\), \(T_0\setminus R\), or \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same lemma shows that
BuildTree descends to proper children and every successful fixing iteration
strictly removes a nonempty bucket.  Thus every deterministic key terminates,
is evaluated once under \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\),
and performs only \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph work.  Equations (11) and
(12) consequently bound all cached graph computation by
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)\right).
 \tag{13}
\]
Finally, each marginalization, product, quotient, and assembly operation is a
constant-arity node of the shared formula DAG.  Constructing and writing these
nodes costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) by the definition of
\(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  Combining this with (13) proves the advertised
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right)
\]
bound.  The argument used only successful terminal calls, so it establishes no
implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification.

Fix the deterministic tie-breaking rule in the statement.  We prove the claim
by unfolding the BuildTree and AttachKernel routines that define sIDP.

Consider a call \(\operatorname{BuildTree}(R,\mathcal P)\).  If its splitting
guard is false, it returns the one-node tree labelled by \(R\).  If the guard
is true, it selects a nonempty \(\mathcal P_R\)-bucket \(B\) and sets
\[
 R_1=\operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}(B),
 \qquad
 R_2=\operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}(R\setminus R_1).
 \tag{14}
\]
The guard itself states \(R_1\subsetneq R\).  Both regions in (14) are subsets
of \(R\), because they are computed in the induced graph \(\mathcal P_R\).
They are nonempty: \(B\subseteq R_1\), while
\(R\setminus R_1\ne\varnothing\) and every vertex belongs to its own region.
We also have \(R_2\subsetneq R\).  Indeed, the elementary closure property in
the definition of a region gives
\[
 B\cap
 \operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}
       \!\left(R\setminus\operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}(B)\right)
 =\varnothing.
 \tag{15}
\]
To verify (15), if a vertex of \(B\) were in the displayed second region, a
pc-connecting path witnessing that membership, concatenated with the
no-arrowhead path witnessing membership in the bucket \(B\), would place its
starting vertex in \(\operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}(B)\), contrary to its
membership in \(R\setminus\operatorname{re}_{\mathcal P_R}(B)\).  Since
\(B\ne\varnothing\), (15) excludes at least one vertex of \(R\) from \(R_2\).
Thus each recursive call is on a proper nonempty subset of its parent.  In
particular, every recursive chain strictly decreases cardinality, and all
graph-only information required by such a call is determined by the single
key \(R\subseteq V\) together with the fixed graph and tie-breaking rule.

Now consider AttachKernel.  At an internal assembly-tree node it only invokes
itself on the two already determined child subtrees, passing the same ambient
set and kernel.  At a leaf labelled \(R\), it initializes a current set
\(T_0\supseteq R\).  Its while-guard selects a
\(\mathcal P_{T_0}\)-bucket \(B\) satisfying
\[
 \varnothing\ne B\subseteq T_0\setminus R.
 \tag{16}
\]
On a successful iteration its set update is exactly
\[
 T_1=T_0\setminus B.
 \tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)--(17) imply
\[
 R\subseteq T_1\subsetneq T_0,
 \qquad |T_1|=|T_0|-|B|<|T_0|.
 \tag{18}
\]
Therefore at most \(|V|-|R|\) successful fixing iterations are possible.
The next guard, the chosen bucket, the possible-descendant and pc-component
sets, and the terminal test \(T_0=R\) are all computed from
\((\mathcal P,R,T_0)\).  With deterministic tie-breaking, the graph-only
fixing subproblem is consequently determined by the key
\((R,T_0)\) with \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  This proves both the claimed
strict progress and the asserted cache-key characterization directly from the
two routines.

proposed.statement:
For a fixed deterministic choice rule, sIDP first decomposes every requested
observed region only into proper region children. At a terminal region
\(R\), its fixing routine has a current set \(T_0\supseteq R\) and every
successful iteration removes a nonempty bucket from \(T_0\). Consequently
every graph-only recursive or fixing subproblem is determined by either a
region \(R\subseteq V\) or a pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a family satisfying Definitions \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family} and \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}.  In particular, \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\), the represented coordinates \(\mathcal M,\mathcal G,F,F'\) and \(R_F\) are fixed, and exactly one normalized local table is changed from \(\theta\) to \(\theta+t v\), where \(v=R_Tq\in T\).  All state spaces used by this certificate are finite and binary by Definition \texttt{def:rational-binary-class}; the target model class itself remains the published positive discrete class.

We first establish exact affinity.  Fix either the observational regime or the terminal regime \(\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\), and fix a complete assignment \(\omega\) of the nonintervened endogenous and latent variables.  In the truncated SCM factorization, the varied local table contributes either one coordinate \(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\), or no coordinate if its endogenous variable is intervened upon.  Every other factor is fixed.  Consequently the complete-assignment mass has one of the two forms
\[
 p_t(\omega)
 =\bigl(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\bigr)
   \prod_{\ell\ne j(\omega)}p_\ell(\omega)
 =p_0(\omega)+t\dot p(\omega)
\]
or \(p_t(\omega)=p_0(\omega)\).  Marginalization is a finite sum, so there are rational directional coefficients, linear in \(v\), such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 o_z(t)&=o_z(0)+t\dot o_z(v),&
 Z_o(t)&=Z_o(0)+t\dot Z_o(v),\\
 h(t)&=h(0)+t\dot h(v),&
 k(t)&=k(0)+t\dot k(v),&
 Z_x(t)&=Z_x(0)+t\dot Z_x(v).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
This proves, rather than assumes, the affine property used below.  Strict positivity of the base mechanisms implies
\[
 Z_o(0)>0,\qquad Z_x(0)>0,\qquad h(0)>0.             \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, each is a finite sum containing positive complete-assignment masses, and the event defining \(h(0)\) is a supported assignment of the positive discrete model.

For every \(t\) for which the perturbed model remains positive, cross-multiplication in (1) gives, cell by cell,
\[
 \frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)}-\frac{o_z(0)}{Z_o(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_o(0)\dot o_z(v)-o_z(0)\dot Z_o(v)\}}
        {Z_o(t)Z_o(0)},                               \tag{3}
\]
and similarly
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-D_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{h(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{h(0)}{Z_x(0)}\\
 &=\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot h(v)-h(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)},                               \tag{4}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-N_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{k(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{k(0)}{Z_x(0)}\\
 &=\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot k(v)-k(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)}.                               \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
The possible products of two slopes cancel in each difference, so (3)--(5) are exact identities, not first-order approximations.  By Definition \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}, after writing \(v=R_Tq\), all braces in (3), followed by the brace in (4), form \(E_Tq\), whereas the brace in (5) is \(b_Tq\).

We next prove the rank criterion over \(\mathbb Q\).  If \(b_T\) is in the row space of \(E_T\), then \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  Conversely, suppose \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  The formula
\[
 \ell(E_Tq)=b_Tq                                             \tag{6}
\]
defines a rational linear functional on \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\), because two preimages of the same vector differ by an element of \(\ker(E_T)\).  Extend a rational basis of \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\) to a basis of its ambient rational vector space and extend \(\ell\) arbitrarily on the added basis vectors.  Then (6) says that \(b_T=\ell E_T\), so \(b_T\) is in the row space of \(E_T\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}:\ E_Tq=0\ \text{ and }\ b_Tq\ne0\\
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow b_T\notin\operatorname{row}(E_T)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T).                              \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]
Rational row reduction decides (7) and, in the strict-rank case, returns a rational null vector \(q\) with \(b_Tq\ne0\).

The criterion does not depend on the chosen rational basis of \(T\).  If \(R_T'\) is another basis matrix, then \(R_T'=R_TH\) for an invertible rational matrix \(H\).  Hence
\[
 ER_T'=E_TH,\qquad bR_T'=b_TH.                            \tag{8}
\]
Right multiplication by \(H\) preserves both ranks in (7), and the coordinate change \(q'=H^{-1}q\) preserves the mechanism direction \(R_T'q'=R_Tq\).  This proves basis independence.

It remains to choose an interval that preserves both positivity and membership in the represented model class.  For the returned \(q\), put \(v=R_Tq\).  Since \(b_Tq=bv\ne0\), one has \(v\ne0\).  Define the positive rational simplex radius
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{pos}}
 =\frac12\min_{j:v_j\ne0}
 \left\{\frac{\theta_j}{|v_j|},
             \frac{1-\theta_j}{|v_j|}\right\}.          \tag{9}
\]
Because \(v\in T\), its coordinates sum to zero in every probability block.  Thus \(\theta+t v\) is normalized, and (9) implies \(0<\theta_j+t v_j<1\) for every coordinate whenever \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{pos}}\).

Positivity alone is not used to infer graph representation.  The parent domains, structural incidence, latent incidence, selection vertices, and all unvaried mechanisms are fixed by Definition \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family}.  No forbidden parent can be introduced because the varied table has the same indexing parent set.  If membership in the represented realization treats parent sets as nonminimal compatibility sets, these facts already preserve \(\mathcal G\).  If the representation convention requires every displayed parent to remain active, let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of displayed parent incidences whose activity is witnessed in the varied table.  Since \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) realizes \(\mathcal G\), for each \(a\in\mathcal A\) choose two entries, differing only in the value of that parent while the other arguments and the child value are fixed, for which
\[
 \alpha_a=\theta_{j_a}-\theta_{j_a'}\ne0.
\]
Put \(\beta_a=v_{j_a}-v_{j_a'}\) and define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{act}}
 =\begin{cases}
  1,&\text{if }\beta_a=0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A,\\
  \displaystyle\min\!\left\{1,
       \frac12\min_{a:\beta_a\ne0}\frac{|\alpha_a|}{|\beta_a|}\right\},
       &\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}                                               \tag{10}
\]
For \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{act}}\),
\[
 |\alpha_a+t\beta_a|
 \ge |\alpha_a|-|t|\,|\beta_a|>\frac12|\alpha_a|>0        \tag{11}
\]
whenever \(\beta_a\ne0\), while the contrast is unchanged when \(\beta_a=0\).  Thus every required active parent stays active.  Equations (10)--(11), together with the unchanged structural and latent incidence, show directly that the perturbed SCM has the same represented graph \(\mathcal G\), hence remains represented by \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\).  Set
\[
 \delta=\min\{\delta_{\mathrm{pos}},\delta_{\mathrm{act}}\}. \tag{12}
\]
All quantities in (9)--(12) are rational and computable from the supplied tables.  For every rational \(t\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\), the perturbed mechanisms are rational, normalized, strictly positive, binary, and compatible with the same represented realization.  Therefore, by Definition \texttt{def:rational-binary-class},
\[
 \mathbf M(0),\mathbf M(t)
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P).                    \tag{13}
\]

Assume now that the equivalent conditions in (7) hold and take any rational \(t\) in the interval (12).  Let \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\).  Since all normalizers in (3)--(5) are positive, \(E_Tq=0\) and (3)--(4) yield
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}
 =P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1},
 \qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}>0.            \tag{14}
\]
The equality of the observational laws in (14) holds for every full observed cell \(z\), hence for the entire normalized selected observational law.  On the other hand, \(b_Tq\ne0\), \(t\ne0\), and (5) give
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}\ne N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}.           \tag{15}
\]
By Definitions \texttt{def:target-query} and \texttt{def:locked-certificate}, the normalized terminal conditional is
\[
 Q_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y;\bar x,\bar c)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
                         \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf1)
 =\frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
        {D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)}.              \tag{16}
\]
Thus (14)--(16) make the two terminal conditionals unequal.

The legal trace contained in the locked certificate starts at \(\rho_0=(X,C)\) and ends at \(\rho\), by Definition \texttt{def:reachable-role-graph}.  At each edge, the moved nonempty role intersection satisfies the stated Chen--Mooij Rule--2 separation.  Apply \texttt{lem:selected-rule-two} with its outcome set equal to \(Y\), its exchange set equal to that moved intersection, and its remaining action and conditioning sets equal to the current role sets.  Its positivity premise holds by (13).  The two adjacent conditional kernels are therefore equal.  Induction over the finite trace gives, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 Q_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(y;\bar x,\bar c)
 =Q_{\rho_0,\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c).                              \tag{17}
\]
Equations (15)--(17) imply \(\psi_{\mathbf M_0}\ne\psi_{\mathbf M_1}\), whereas (14) gives equality of their full selected observational laws.  Since the pair lies in the rational binary subclass in (13), it is also a pair in the published class quantified over by Definition \texttt{def:identification}; the negative conclusion therefore transfers upward to that class.  No positive completeness transfer from the binary subclass is being asserted.  The supplied represented graph, forest, and trace satisfy the remaining clauses of Definition \texttt{def:locked-certificate}, so \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns the claimed \(\Gamma\).

Finally, we prove the complexity bounds in the stated expanded encodings.  Clear denominators in \(E_T\) and \(b_T\), and use fraction-free Gaussian elimination.  If the integerized matrix has dimensions bounded by \(s\) and input entries of bit length at most \(B\), every elimination value is a minor of an input submatrix.  The Leibniz formula bounds the absolute value of an \(r\)-by-\(r\) minor by \(r!2^{rB}\), so its bit length is at most
\[
 rB+\log_2(r!)+1=O\bigl(s(B+\log s)\bigr).              \tag{18}
\]
There are polynomially many arithmetic operations, and (18) bounds their bit sizes polynomially.  The rank test, a rational null vector, the active-parent witnesses, (9)--(12), and a choice such as \(t=\delta/2\) are consequently computable in polynomial time in \(L_{\mathrm{temp}}\).

The compiler then copies the supplied graph, trace, and forest data and enumerates the dense complete-assignment tables.  Each displayed atom is obtained by a product of encoded local probabilities and each displayed marginal by a sum over entries that are themselves part of the expanded output.  Sequential exact products and sums have bit length polynomial in the total input-plus-output bit length.  Hence compilation, including writing \(\Gamma\), takes \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.

For verification, acyclicity, ancestry, latent projection, endpoint compatibility, role-edge legality, and the forest predicates are finite incidence or reachability checks.  If a representation convention is verified through its full separation model, an exhaustive check is still polynomial in the expanded certificate length: the dense observed table already has at least \(2^n\) entries, while the collection of disjoint vertex triples has at most \(4^n\) members.  The verifier checks every probability block for exact normalization and strict positivity, checks the active-parent witnesses from (11), recomputes the displayed observational and interventional atoms from the dense rational factorization, and verifies (14)--(15) by exact cross-multiplication.  The number and bit length of all inputs to these operations are bounded by \(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma}\).  Therefore \(\operatorname{Verify}\) runs in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, completing the proof.

proposed.statement: For every rational interior one-mechanism affine family, the following are equivalent: \(\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\) with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\); and \(\operatorname{rank}([E_T;b_T])>\operatorname{rank}(E_T)\). The condition is independent of the rational basis \(R_T\). Whenever it holds, rational row reduction yields \(v=R_Tq\), and there is a computable \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that every \(t\in\mathbb Q\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) keeps \(\theta+t v\) normalized and strictly positive, preserves the entire normalized selected observational law and \(D_{\rho}\) exactly, and changes \(N_{\rho}\). Thus \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns a positive rational pair certifying nonidentification of \(\psi\) in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) checks the expanded certificate in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
proposed.justification: The theorem turns a numerical or symbolic fiber direction into an exact, portable, positive rational causal nonidentification certificate.
proposed.gap: Discrete polynomial programs describe observational fibers, but the checked literature does not isolate an exact simplex-tangent criterion that simultaneously locks a selected conditional denominator and separates its numerator.
proposed.consumer: A graph search or algebraic solver can hand one passing template to the compiler and obtain a certificate that a third party verifies without trusting the search.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the reachable-role-state definition and the already-established selected Rule--2 theorem that the proof uses to transport terminal conditional disagreement back to the original query.
